newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA, TURKEY TO BOOST ENERGY COOPERATION.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA, TURKEY TO BOOST ENERGY COOPERATION.

text.p: Bulgaria and Turkey have signed a five year agreement aimed at boosting cooperation in the energy field, the chairman of Bulgaria's National Electricity Company (NEC) said on Wednesday.

Kozma Kuzmanov, who headed the Bulgarian delegation to Turkey, said the agreement signed by the NEC and the Turkish Electricity Generation and Transmission Company last week, envisaged increasing Bulgarian electricity supplies to Turkey.
Bulgaria now exports 300-400 megawatts of electricity per month to neighbouring Turkey and its monthly income from these exports is some $10 million, energy officials said.

"Apart from the cooperation agreement, we also signed a protocol under which former schemes for energy supplies from Maritsa East will be renewed," Kuzmanov told Reuters, referring to Bulgaria's biggest mining and thermal power complex. He did not give further details.

A delegation of the Turkish company, which is struggling to meet the country's growing electricity demand, will visit Bulgaria's Kozloduy nuclear power plant and the site of a second nuclear plant at Belene in the beginning of April.

Bulgaria, which relies on nuclear power for more than 40 percent of its energy needs, may complete its Belene plant, where work on its construction was stopped in 1990 due to a shortage of cash and environmentalists' protests.
The foundations of the plant have been built up and a 1,000-megawatt Soviet-designed reactor is on site. Some $1 billion has been invested there.
